statement: For either sign, form H_(N,q)=sum_(k<N) q^(N-1-k)*K_k with 0<=q<1 and normalize by its finite supremum M_(N,q), where N>=1. If q^N is at most every unit value of the complete table K_N, then that floor is at most 3/4 and 1-q>=1/(4N). Also M_(N,q)>=(3/2)^(N-1). At any fixed nonperiodic positive odd root a, H_(N,q)(a)<=A_s(a)*N^2, hence (H_(N,q)(a)/M_(N,q))/(1-q)<=4*A_s(a)*N^3*(2/3)^(N-1). For every sequence of rates satisfying the block-minimum premise, this ratio tends to zero. This closes that specific construction of near-critical minorants; it does not exclude arbitrary periodic weights, a different rate certificate for the same table, actual coefficient divergence, or imply Juggler termination. For either signed odd Collatz map and every nonperiodic positive odd root a, each unit-supported finite exponent budget B is at most a*D_s times the harmonic sum through a*2^B, where D_+=1 and D_-=exp(reciprocalBudget) is the existing absolute distortion constant. Thus K_d(a)<=a*D_s*(1+log a+8*d*log 2)+(19683/32768)^d<=A_s(a)*(d+1), with A_s(a)=a*D_s*(1+log a+8*log 2)+1>=1. The complete all-source coefficient satisfies C_d(a)<=(21/5)*A_s(a)*(d+1). These are upper bounds at a fixed ordinary root, not uniform bounds over root heights, lower counts, summability or termination results.
